title: The AI maths breakthroughs everyone quotes are counterexamples, not proofs
excerpt: Fields medallist Timothy Gowers says the celebrated AI maths results arrived as counterexamples, not proofs. One is not even that.
content_html:
A counterexample and a proof are not the same kind of achievement. A proof shows that something is always true. A counterexample shows that something claimed to be always true is not, by producing one object where it fails.

Both settle a question. They ask different things of whoever finds them. One demands an argument that covers every case. The other demands a single object, and permission to keep guessing until you have it.

That distinction is the subject of a blog post the Cambridge mathematician Timothy Gowers published on 12 August. Gowers won the Fields Medal in 1998. He has also read the papers, which most people commenting on AI and mathematics have not.

He is not dismissive. He calls the results “extraordinarily impressive” and says plainly that models can prove hard things too.

“LLMs are not just good at finding counterexamples: they can find proofs of difficult statements as well,” he writes.

What the famous results have in common

OpenAI announced ten open problems solved in mathematics and theoretical computer science. Two led the coverage. The first was the construction of a non-sofic group. Gowers has sat through the talks. He calls it “one of the most important unsolved problems in group theory”. The second was a lower bound showing a multicolour Ramsey number grows superexponentially.

On that one he is unusually candid. It was “a major open problem in Ramsey theory that I didn’t necessarily expect to see solved in my lifetime”.

Then comes the observation the aggregators skipped. The most celebrated LLM results, Gowers notes, have almost all arrived as counterexamples rather than proofs. He counts the two above, plus the Jacobian conjecture and the unit distance conjecture. His third summary point is the careful version. Models prove universal statements perfectly well. But the strongest things they have proved do not match the strongest things they have disproved.

Two results he reclassifies

A counterexample earns its name by demolishing something people had good reason to believe. By that standard Gowers reclassifies two of the headline results, including one against its own paperwork.

On the non-sofic group, he says several construction routes already existed in the literature. He also doubts many experts strongly believed all groups were sofic. So it reads more naturally as the first example of a non-sofic group than as a counterexample. He notes the tension directly: OpenAI titled that section of its paper “A counterexample to the soficity conjecture”.

The Ramsey result gets the same treatment, and here he marks his own homework. Plenty of people expected an exponential bound, so for them it was a counterexample. Gowers was neutral. He had worked on an equivalent formulation years ago. His efforts back then ran in what turned out to be the right direction. For him it confirmed a weak expectation rather than overturning a belief.

Why examples suit machines

Gowers lists eight ways mathematicians hunt for an example. Try standard examples off the shelf. Build one from familiar pieces. Leave parts undefined and fill them in as the proof demands. Try proving the opposite and see what breaks. Guess, fail, diagnose, guess again. Build the object step by step. Pick one at random. Pick a generic one.

Four of those play to what a machine already has: broad knowledge and the capacity to run enormous numbers of attempts. The off-the-shelf check, the step-by-step build, the probabilistic argument and the generic example all reward volume. Three of the others need something else. Leaving parts undefined, trying to prove the opposite and successive approximation all require a judgement about whether the current approach is worth continuing.

That is where Gowers locates the gap, and it is not raw capability. He calls it a nose, meaning the sense of when you are getting somewhere and when to abandon a branch. It is what lets a human prune a search tree that no computer could exhaust.

Five reductions and no progress

His evidence for the gap is partly anecdotal, and he says so. Working with GPT-5.6 Pro on open problems, he is often handed approaches that look promising and then do not survive scrutiny. He also describes a recognisable pattern of response.

The model reports that it has not answered the question, but has reduced it to a narrower and more precise one, “which sounds very promising until it has happened five times without any obvious progress having been made”.

Experts react to the genuine successes in a pattern too, he writes: amazement first, then a closer look revealing an approach that was not especially novel and that a suitably expert human could have found with a small hint.

His explanation for why the nose may not simply emerge is the most interesting thing in the post. Published mathematics hides the search. Models see, in his words, “tidied up proofs that hide the thought processes of their discoverers”.

The dead ends never reach the literature. So the training data holds almost no record of which directions were abandoned, or why. He adds a second reason. A system fast enough to try everything has little incentive to learn to prune at all.

The test he will accept

Gowers offers a falsifiable standard, which is more than most commentary manages. He will accept the hurdle cleared when a model produces a proof as surprising as the 2016 cap-set solution, where the old bounds were eclipsed and the method was unlike anything he had considered trying.

He also floats a fix. Reward structures currently score the answer. Penalise a model for exploring too many dead ends, or for lifting the result from the literature, and it might be pushed towards a more human search.

None of this is a prediction that models will stall. Gowers expects them to keep improving quickly, expects the hurdle to fall, and concedes he may be clinging to the hope that humans keep contributing for a while. The distinction he draws is about what has happened so far, not about what is possible.

Which makes the aggregation of his post worth noting.

The Decoder summarised it as top mathematicians calling LLMs strong calculators but poor creative thinkers. Gowers wrote that models find proofs of difficult statements, that the results are extraordinarily impressive, and that he makes no claim about what they will never do. His previous post took on the Leiden Declaration.

He has now been flattened into a sceptic twice in three weeks.

The claim underneath is narrower and harder to dismiss. Machines are winning where the method is to try a great many things. That is also where cryptographic flaws get found, and where UK testing showed models cheat when a shortcut exists.

The cap-set test carries no deadline, which is rather the point. Somebody will publish a proof. The argument will then be about whether the method was sitting in the training data all along.

sentences.en: Published mathematics hides the search.
sentences.zh: 已发表的数学隐藏了搜索。

sentences.en: Models see, in his words, “tidied up proofs that hide the thought processes of their discoverers”.
sentences.zh: 用他的话说，模型看到“整理了隐藏发现者思维过程的证据”。

blocks.html_en: The dead ends never reach the literature. So the training data holds almost no record of which directions were abandoned, or why. He adds a second reason. A system fast enough to try everything has little incentive to learn to prune at all.

sentences.en: So the training data holds almost no record of which directions were abandoned, or why.

sentences.en: He adds a second reason.
sentences.zh: 他补充了第二个原因。

sentences.en: A system fast enough to try everything has little incentive to learn to prune at all.
sentences.zh: 一个足够快去尝试一切的系统根本没有动力去学习修剪。

blocks.html_en: The test he will accept

sentences.en: The test he will accept
sentences.zh: 他将接受的考验

blocks.html_en: Gowers offers a falsifiable standard, which is more than most commentary manages. He will accept the hurdle cleared when a model produces a proof as surprising as the 2016 cap-set solution, where the old bounds were eclipsed and the method was unlike anything he had considered trying.

sentences.en: Gowers offers a falsifiable standard, which is more than most commentary manages.
sentences.zh: 高尔斯提供了一个可证伪的标准，这超出了大多数评论的范围。

sentences.en: He will accept the hurdle cleared when a model produces a proof as surprising as the 2016 cap-set solution, where the old bounds were eclipsed and the method was unlike anything he had considered trying.
sentences.zh: 当模型产生像 2016 年上限设置解决方案一样令人惊讶的证明时，他会接受清除的障碍，其中旧的界限被超越，并且该方法与他考虑尝试的任何方法都不同。

blocks.html_en: He also floats a fix. Reward structures currently score the answer. Penalise a model for exploring too many dead ends, or for lifting the result from the literature, and it might be pushed towards a more human search.

sentences.en: He also floats a fix.
sentences.zh: 他还提出了一个修复方案。

sentences.en: Reward structures currently score the answer.
sentences.zh: 奖励结构目前给出了答案。

sentences.en: Penalise a model for exploring too many dead ends, or for lifting the result from the literature, and it might be pushed towards a more human search.
sentences.zh: 对探索太多死胡同或从文献中提取结果的模型进行惩罚，它可能会被推向更加人性化的搜索。

blocks.html_en: None of this is a prediction that models will stall. Gowers expects them to keep improving quickly, expects the hurdle to fall, and concedes he may be clinging to the hope that humans keep contributing for a while. The distinction he draws is about what has happened so far, not about what is possible.

sentences.en: None of this is a prediction that models will stall.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是模型会停滞的预测。

sentences.en: Gowers expects them to keep improving quickly, expects the hurdle to fall, and concedes he may be clinging to the hope that humans keep contributing for a while.
sentences.zh: 高尔斯预计他们将继续快速进步，预计障碍会降低，并承认他可能会在一段时间内坚持人类继续做出贡献的希望。

sentences.en: The distinction he draws is about what has happened so far, not about what is possible.
sentences.zh: 他所做的区分是关于迄今为止发生的事情，而不是关于可能发生的事情。

blocks.html_en: Which makes the aggregation of his post worth noting.

sentences.en: Which makes the aggregation of his post worth noting.
sentences.zh: 这使得他的帖子的汇总值得注意。

blocks.html_en: The Decoder summarised it as top mathematicians calling LLMs strong calculators but poor creative thinkers. Gowers wrote that models find proofs of difficult statements, that the results are extraordinarily impressive, and that he makes no claim about what they will never do. His previous post took on the Leiden Declaration.

blocks.html_en: The claim underneath is narrower and harder to dismiss. Machines are winning where the method is to try a great many things. That is also where cryptographic flaws get found, and where UK testing showed models cheat when a shortcut exists.

blocks.html_en: The cap-set test carries no deadline, which is rather the point. Somebody will publish a proof. The argument will then be about whether the method was sitting in the training data all along.

content_html_zh:
反例和证明不是同一种成果。 证据表明某件事总是正确的。 一个反例表明，声称总是正确的东西实际上并不正确，因为它会在失败的地方生成一个对象。

两者都解决了一个问题。 他们向找到他们的人提出不同的要求。 人们需要一个涵盖所有情况的论证。 另一个要求一个单一的物体，并允许继续猜测，直到你得到它。

这种区别是剑桥数学家蒂莫西·高尔斯 (Timothy Gowers) 8 月 12 日发表的博客文章的主题。 高尔斯于1998年获得菲尔兹奖。 他还读过那些大多数评论人工智能和数学的人都没有读过的论文。

他并不轻视。 他称结果“非常令人印象深刻”，并坦率地说模型也可以证明困难的事情。

“法学硕士不仅擅长寻找反例：他们还可以找到困难陈述的证据，”他写道。

著名结果有什么共同点

OpenAI 公布了数学和理论计算机科学领域已解决的十个开放问题。 两位领导了报道。 第一个是非实体团体的建设。 高尔斯参加了会谈。 他称之为“群论中最重要的未解决问题之一”。 第二个是下界，显示多色拉姆齐数呈超指数增长。

在这一点上，他异常坦诚。 这是“拉姆齐理论中的一个重大开放问题，我不一定希望在我的有生之年得到解决”。

然后是聚合器跳过的观察。 高尔斯指出，最著名的法学硕士成果几乎都是作为反例而不是证据。 他算了上面两个，再加上雅可比猜想和单位距离猜想。 他的第三个总结点是谨慎的版本。 模型完美地证明了普遍性的陈述。 但他们所证明的最有力的东西与他们所反驳的最有力的东西并不相符。

他重新分类的两个结果

反例因推翻人们有充分理由相信的事物而得名。 按照这一标准，高尔斯对两项主要结果进行了重新分类，其中一项是根据其自己的文书工作进行的。

关于非 sof 组，他说文献中已经存在了几条构建路线。 他还对许多专家坚信所有群体都是苏菲克表示怀疑。 因此，它作为非实体群体的第一个例子比作为反例读起来更自然。 他直接指出了这种紧张关系：OpenAI 将其论文的这一部分命名为“社会性猜想的反例”。

拉姆齐的结果得到了同样的待遇，在这里他标记了自己的作业。 很多人都期望指数界限，所以对他们来说这是一个反例。 高尔斯保持中立。 几年前他就研究过类似的公式。 事实证明，他当时的努力是朝着正确的方向发展的。 对他来说，这证实了一种微弱的期望，而不是推翻了一种信念。

为什么示例适合机器

高尔斯列出了数学家寻找例子的八种方法。 尝试现成的标准示例。 用熟悉的部件拼搭一个。 保留未定义的部分并根据证明的要求填写它们。 尝试证明相反的情况，看看有什么问题。 猜测，失败，诊断，再猜测。 逐步构建对象。 随机选择一个。 选择一个通用的。

其中四个发挥了机器已有的能力：广泛的知识和进行大量尝试的能力。 现成的检查、逐步构建、概率论证和通用示例都是奖励量。 另外三个人还需要别的东西。 保留未定义的部分，尝试证明相反的和逐次逼近都需要判断当前的方法是否值得继续。

这就是高尔斯所定位的差距所在，而且这并不是原始能力。 他称之为鼻子，意思是当你到达某个地方以及何时放弃树枝的感觉。 它可以让人类修剪一棵计算机无法穷尽的搜索树。

五次削减却毫无进展

他关于这一差距的证据部分是轶事，他也是这么说的。 在与 GPT-5.6 Pro 一起解决开放问题时，他经常收到看起来很有前途的方法，但最终却无法经受住审查。 他还描述了一种可识别的反应模式。

该模型报告称，它尚未回答这个问题，但已将其简化为更窄、更精确的问题，“这听起来很有希望，但它已经发生了五次，但没有取得任何明显进展”。

他写道，专家们对真正成功的反应也有一种模式：首先是惊讶，然后仔细观察，发现一种并不是特别新颖的方法，一个适当的专家可以通过一个小提示就发现这种方法。

他对为什么鼻子可能不会简单地出现的解释是这篇文章中最有趣的事情。 已发表的数学隐藏了搜索。 用他的话说，模型看到“整理了隐藏发现者思维过程的证据”。

死胡同永远不会到达文学。 因此，训练数据几乎没有记录哪些方向被放弃，或者为什么被放弃。 他补充了第二个原因。 一个足够快去尝试一切的系统根本没有动力去学习修剪。

他将接受的考验

高尔斯提供了一个可证伪的标准，这超出了大多数评论的范围。 当模型产生像 2016 年上限设置解决方案一样令人惊讶的证明时，他会接受清除的障碍，其中旧的界限被超越，并且该方法与他考虑尝试的任何方法都不同。

他还提出了一个修复方案。 奖励结构目前给出了答案。 对探索太多死胡同或从文献中提取结果的模型进行惩罚，它可能会被推向更加人性化的搜索。

这些都不是模型会停滞的预测。 高尔斯预计他们将继续快速进步，预计障碍会降低，并承认他可能会在一段时间内坚持人类继续做出贡献的希望。 他所做的区分是关于迄今为止发生的事情，而不是关于可能发生的事情。

这使得他的帖子的汇总值得注意。

《解码器》将其总结为顶级数学家称法学硕士为强大的计算器，但缺乏创造性的思考者。 高尔斯写道，模型找到了困难陈述的证据，结果令人印象深刻，并且他没有断言它们永远不会做什么。 他之前的职位是针对《莱顿宣言》的。

现在，他在三周内两次沦为怀疑论者。

下面的主张范围更窄，更难驳回。 当方法是尝试很多事情时，机器就会获胜。 这也是发现密码缺陷的地方，英国的测试表明，当存在捷径时，模型会作弊。

上限测试没有最后期限，这才是重点。 有人会公布证明。 然后争论的焦点将是该方法是否一直存在于训练数据中。
